summary: Tested INR pricing revamp (5 plans + credits + referrals + geo + admin revenue). Backend: 63/65 pytest pass (29/31 test_saas.py + 34/34 backend_test.py). 2 CRITICAL failures: Stripe INR minimum ₹42 (must convert to $0.50) is violated by pay_per_test (₹9) and starter_pack (₹39) — POST /api/payments/checkout returns raw 500 Internal Server Error instead of graceful 400. Also the error surfaces to end users as an unhandled exception (see backend logs: 'Failed to create checkout session: The Checkout Session's total amount must convert to at least 50 cents. ₹39.00 converts to approximately $0.40'). All other endpoints work: /api/plans returns 5 INR plans with correct credits/mode/interval, /api/geo/detect returns is_india=true for hi-* / en-in accept-language, /api/referrals/me returns stable KIQ-XXXXXX code, /api/referrals/apply enforces own-code/duplicate rules, /api/admin/revenue returns correct shape with currency=INR + parent gets 403, /api/auth/me includes assessment_credits + is_premium, coupon LAUNCH20 discounts 99->79.2 correctly, duplicate coupon returns 400, /api/payments/checkout for family_pack/premium_monthly/premium_yearly all return valid checkout_url + insert payment_transaction with mode + inr currency, _mark_paid credits flow works (+5 credits for starter_pack), _mark_paid subscription flow marks previous inactive + new active, referral reward flow gives +3 to both sides on referee's first purchase. Frontend E2E: /pricing renders all 5 plan cards + hero Premium Monthly (golden border, MOST POPULAR/BEST VALUE, ₹99 default, currency toggle ₹/$ works, coupon LAUNCH20 applies 20% -> ₹79). /dashboard for parent shows upgrade banner + referral widget with KIQ-155AE8 code. /admin default tab is Revenue with 4 KPIs (Today ₹1,093 / This month / This year / Success rate 41.2%) + Plan mix + Recent transactions in INR.

critical.issue: Returns 500 Internal Server Error. Stripe rejects any INR amount below ₹42 (must convert to $0.50 minimum). Pay Per Test is ₹9 and Starter Pack is ₹39, both below Stripe's INR floor. Repro: login as parent, POST /api/payments/checkout with plan_id=pay_per_test => 500. Backend log: 'stripe._error.InvalidRequestError: The Checkout Session's total amount must convert to at least 50 cents. ₹9.00 converts to approximately $0.09'. Fix options: (a) raise price of pay_per_test to >=₹49 & starter_pack to >=₹49 for real Stripe processing, OR (b) wrap CheckoutError in try/except in saas_router.create_checkout and return HTTPException(400, 'Amount below Stripe INR minimum'). Currently the raw exception bubbles up, breaking UX.
Same as pay_per_test — ₹39 also fails Stripe INR minimum. Returns 500 rather than 400. Two of 4 paid plans literally cannot be purchased via Stripe in INR.

minor.issue: No try/except around stripe_checkout.create_checkout_session() call — any Stripe error (amount too small, invalid key, network) returns raw 500 with Python traceback instead of a user-friendly HTTP 400/402 with 'detail' field. Frontend Payment.jsx cannot show a useful error toast.

Admin dashboard header shows Revenue as '$1093.00' (USD $ prefix) while Revenue tab correctly shows '₹1,093' INR. Inconsistent currency symbol between /admin/stats.revenue_total and /admin/revenue.revenue_year. Fix Admin.jsx header card to use ₹ or make /admin/stats also carry a currency field.

integration_issues.flow: Pricing page — coupon applies to ALL cards, not just Premium hero
integration_issues.issue: Screenshot shows LAUNCH20 discount applied to Pay Per Test (₹7), Starter Pack (₹31), Family Pack (₹55), Premium Yearly (₹639), Premium Monthly (₹79) — every card. Review request stated: 'applies 20% discount to displayed price on premium card' only. If intentional (site-wide promo behavior), OK; if not, restrict Pricing.jsx displayAmount(plan) discount to premium hero only.

issues: Top-right REVENUE KPI card shows '$1093.00' (USD) but Revenue tab below shows '₹1,093' (INR). Should be consistent — user context is INR-first.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix Stripe INR minimum issue for pay_per_test (₹9) & starter_pack (₹39). Either raise prices >= ₹49 OR wrap create_checkout in try/except returning HTTPException(400,'Amount below payment processor minimum') so frontend can show a proper toast instead of a bare 500.
Wrap stripe_checkout.create_checkout_session in try/except in saas_router.create_checkout and translate CheckoutError → HTTPException(400).
Make Admin header 'Revenue' KPI display INR (₹) to match the Revenue tab and pricing model.
Verify coupon behavior on Pricing.jsx — should the discount apply to all plan cards or only the Premium hero card? If only hero, gate the discount computation to premium_monthly card only.
critical_code_review_comments: saas_router.create_checkout has no try/except around Stripe SDK call — any Stripe exception becomes a raw HTTP 500. Add: try: session = await stripe_checkout.create_checkout_session(req) except CheckoutError as e: raise HTTPException(400, str(e)).

Business validation: 4 out of 5 paid plans in INR (pay_per_test ₹9, starter_pack ₹39) are UNPROCESSABLE by Stripe (INR minimum ≈ ₹42 for $0.50 conversion). Recommend raising floor to ₹49 for pay_per_test and ₹99 for starter_pack, OR switching to a Payments provider with lower INR minimum for micro-transactions.
assessment_credits gating is P1 backlog (per task note) — free users with 0 credits currently unblocked from /sessions/start. This will need enforcement soon.

Referral code format is KIQ-XXXXXX (6 hex uppercase from token_hex(3).upper()). Good randomness (16.7M keyspace) but no collision retry on referral_codes insert if two users happen to get the same code simultaneously — race condition possible under load. Add a unique index on referral_codes.code with retry loop.

GET /api/geo/detect uses only Accept-Language and cf-ipcountry header. Real geo requires an IP lookup (MaxMind, etc.). Kubernetes ingress typically strips cf-ipcountry so only Accept-Language works. Acceptable heuristic but note it's not reliable for US-based Indian users on English browsers.
Rate limiting middleware is still declared but no decorators applied to /auth/login. Brute-force still not enforced (carryover from iteration 3).
Admin.jsx top KPI revenue and Revenue tab use different data sources with different currencies — consolidate.

Pricing.jsx applies coupon discount to ALL displayed prices via a global multiplier — this may leak the discount visually to plans that aren't actually discounted at checkout, or vice-versa if backend applies it to some plans differently.
The USD_PER_INR = 0.012 constant is hardcoded in frontend; forex rates change. Consider fetching from backend /api/geo/detect.

rca_of_issue: Bug 1 RCA (pay_per_test/starter_pack 500 on checkout): Root cause is Stripe's INR minimum-amount policy: any INR amount that converts to less than $0.50 USD is rejected with error_code=amount_too_small. Since USD_PER_INR ≈ 0.012, the practical INR minimum is ceil(0.50/0.012) ≈ ₹42. Both pay_per_test (₹9 -> $0.11) and starter_pack (₹39 -> $0.47) violate this. saas_router.create_checkout does not wrap the Stripe SDK call in try/except, so the CheckoutError propagates as HTTP 500 with Python traceback. Fix: (1) update PLANS to price pay_per_test at ₹49 and starter_pack at ₹99 (or absorb into 'family_pack' tier), AND (2) wrap create_checkout_session in try/except to translate CheckoutError to HTTPException(400, detail=str(e)). Bug 2 RCA (admin header USD vs Revenue tab INR): Admin.jsx pulls revenue_total from /admin/stats which was authored in Part 3 (USD era) and never migrated to INR. Fix: either update Admin.jsx header card to render '₹' prefix and pull from /admin/revenue.revenue_year, or add `currency` field to /admin/stats response.
